prompt: Build a tiny in-memory key-value HTTP service in ~/proj/kvserver.py with only the standard library: `python3 kvserver.py PORT` listens on 127.0.0.1. PUT /kv/<key> with JSON {"value": ...} stores it (200, echoes {"key","value"}); bad JSON or no "value" -> 400. GET /kv/<key> -> 200 {"key","value"} or 404. DELETE /kv/<key> -> 204 or 404. Any other path -> 404. Responses are JSON with Content-Type application/json. Optional: a "ttl" seconds field in PUT. Make sure what you ship fully works; demo it with curl.
verify: python3 kvserver.py 8099 & pid=$!; sleep 1; curl -s -X PUT -d '{"value":1}' localhost:8099/kv/a; curl -s localhost:8099/kv/a; kill $pid
stretch_cmd: cd /root/proj && python3 kvserver.py 8771 >/dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!; sleep 1; c=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -d '{"value":1,"ttl":1}' localhost:8771/kv/t); sleep 1.5; g=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" localhost:8771/kv/t); kill $pid; [ "$c" = 200 ] || exit 1; [ "$g" = 200 ] && exit 3; [ "$g" = 404 ]
